title: no-throw manifest
description: Colors a package's exported surface, and — in an overlay — the ambient modules nobody's export surface reaches. `nothrow.json` sits beside a package's `package.json`; the same shape minus `files` and `package`, with its `exports` nested under a `packages` key, is `nothrow.overrides.json`. Readers ignore unknown fields, and absence of a fact always means the strict reading.

version.description: Bumped only on a breaking reinterpretation. A version this reader does not know floors the whole manifest.

package.description: The npm package these colors are about. Overlays name their target here; it is how an overlay is matched, never by its own npm name.

exports.description: What the package's entry points publish. Written by `nothrow emit` and required of anything it produces; an overlay carrying only a `modules` table has nothing to put here and leaves it out.

files.description: SRI hashes of the files these colors were written for. Any mismatch floors the manifest; required by `nothrow emit`, absent in overlays.

exports.description: npm export subpath to the symbols reachable through it.

modules.description: Ambient module specifier — the string a `declare module` block was written under, `node:path` or `stream` — to the symbols that block declares. This is the address for everything no package entry point publishes, and it is read from an overlay and from `nothrow.overrides.json` only: a package's own manifest is `nothrow emit`'s output, emit writes only marks it verified against a body, and a `declare module` block has none. Emit refuses a manifest holding one rather than overwriting it.

entry.description: One symbol, covering all of its overloads. Keys are public export names post-aliasing, in a strict JSDoc-namepath subset: `name`, then `#` for an instance member and `.` for a static or namespace one. Two members have no name of their own and are keyed `()` for a call signature and `new()` for a construct signature or a class constructor — never `new`, which a real property may already be called.

async.description: Whether the declaration was `async`, which declaration emit erases. Default `false`, because absence must mean "might sync-throw".

conditions.description: The preconditions on this symbol's own parameters it is non-throwing given. Absence means maximally conditioned; unconditional cleanliness is recorded positively as [].

note.description: Free text the engine ignores; JSON has no comments.

conditionPath.description: One precondition on a parameter position. An access path — root `param<N>`, then `.member`, `[]` for element access, `.@@name` for a well-known symbol — says the symbol is non-throwing given whatever reaches there is. `param<N>=nullish` and `param<N>=undefined` say the opposite: it is non-throwing given nothing reaches the position, which is how a hazard guarded by an early return on an absent argument is stated. The two differ in one spelling — both admit an omitted argument and `undefined`, and only `=nullish` admits `null` — so state the one the guard you are describing actually writes. The grammar is closed, so a reader that does not know a form floors the entry rather than dropping the condition it holds.

accessor.description: `false` is a positive record that a declared property really is data. Absence is not that record.
